codes.descriptor: discuss how characters and settings are connected in literature created by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors and illustrators

elaborations.text: discussing the depiction of characters in particular settings in well-known fairytales from wide-ranging world authors; for example, children in forests, and royalty in castles and towers
recognising recurring characters in particular settings in texts by First Nations Australian authors
exploring the way wide-ranging Australian authors and illustrators depict the Australian outback and the associated characters

entry_focuses: Link characters and settings in named world fairytales
Discuss a recurring guide on specific First Nations Country
Compare Australian journeys and an actual outback spread
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide brief original premises for Rapunzel and Little Red-Cap (Brothers Grimm versions). Actual Cooee Mittigar by Jasmine Seymour/Leanne Mulgo Watson: adult supplies lawful book, two seasonal spreads and glossary; track Mulgo’s recurring guide role in each. Compare named source context, no pan-Nations claim. Are We There Yet? by Alison Lester: adult supplies actual outback spread plus another setting; publisher verifies Grace/family/outback journey. Supplied Penguin synopsis/teacher-method facts only are not full-book or artwork observation. Original evidence chart records title/creators, character, setting, clue and connection.

codes.descriptor: identify features of literary texts, such as characters and settings, and give reasons for personal preferences

elaborations.text: discussing preferences for stories set in familiar or unfamiliar worlds, or about characters whose lives are like or unlike their own
discussing their feelings about the positive and negative behaviours of non-human characters, such as animals

entry_focuses: Identify character and setting features
Explain preferences using a relevant detail
Compare supported preferences and animal behaviour
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide two complete original short stories: a familiar school setting and an imaginary moon garden, with helpful and unhelpful animal actions. Supply four feature cards plus two different supported preference responses. Teach taste is open; text claims still need evidence.

codes.descriptor: discuss the characters and settings of a range of texts and identify how language is used to present these features in different ways

elaborations.text: comparing how similar characters or settings are described in texts from different contexts; for example, how the seasons are described
identifying and comparing verb groups used to convey actions, emotions and dialogue in a range of literary texts
identifying the language used to describe the landscape in First Nations Australians’ stories

entry_focuses: Compare action and dialogue language
Compare setting and seasonal language
Read actual First Nations landscape wording with context
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide complete paired character/dialogue and contrasting seasonal setting passages. Compare whole verb groups and words, not adjective lists alone. Adult stages lawful Cooee Mittigar book and identifies two actual short landscape phrases/spread/glossary before source-specific tasks; do not invent a quotation or infer language from landscape. Nura is sourced Country terminology, not a generic land synonym.

codes.descriptor: identify, reproduce and experiment with rhythmic sound and word patterns in poems, chants, rhymes or songs

elaborations.text: exploring poems, chants, rhymes or songs from different home languages of class members

entry_focuses: Notice sound and repeated word patterns
Reproduce rhythm against a steady pulse
Experiment and compare with a verified home-language model
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide an entire original short rhyme/chant and exact4pulse slot models, including a rest and two short syllables in one pulse. Separate pulse and word rhythm. Model/reproduce/adapt spoken or accessible equivalent output; no paper certification. Adult/family supplies a known permitted home-language rhyme with actual pronunciation/meaning model, without guessing accents/language or compulsory disclosure.

codes.descriptor: create and edit literary texts by adapting structures and language features of familiar literary texts through drawing, writing, performance and digital tools

elaborations.text: inventing some speech, dialogue or behaviour for a favourite character, which may include the use of video and audio tools, for an alternative event or outcome in the original text
reviewing and developing sentences; for example, adding prepositional phrases such as “with a long tail” to improve descriptions

entry_focuses: Adapt a familiar complete story structure
Change speech,description and mode deliberately
Edit for coherent events and present the changed story
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide original complete story with opening/problem/response/ending, a coherent adaptation retaining a pattern, actual out-of-order draft and sentence expansion. Learner produces drawing+caption, writing, performance or adult-approved digital story. No cultural story/art imitation; real actual creation and subsequent editing observed.

codes.descriptor: identify how similar topics and information are presented in different types of texts

elaborations.text: reading a poem, narrative and informative text about lifecycles and discussing what is learnt
exploring recipes presented on food packets, in recipe books, in short video clips and in a digital form, noting their shared purpose

entry_focuses: Compare poem,narrative and information on a life cycle
Sort shared and unique information with complete texts
Compare actual recipe formats and their common purpose
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide complete original frog-cycle poem, narrative and information cards plus explicit shared/unique chart and sequence model. Supply original recipe packet/book/digital layouts. For the video format, adult opens actual named ABC Annaka procedural video on making a vegetable truck (no food handling required); observe movement/order only after actual viewing, or read available transcript with text-only limitation. Contrast the video recipe and each static version; samepurpose does not require sameingredients.

codes.descriptor: use interaction skills when engaging with topics, actively listening to others, receiving instructions and extending own ideas, speaking appropriately, expressing and responding to opinions, making statements, and giving instructions

elaborations.text: exploring ways to comment on what others say, including using sentence starters such as “I like the way you …”, “I agree that …”, “I have a different thought …”, “I’d like to say something different …”
demonstrating appropriate listening behaviours, responding to and paraphrasing a partner’s contribution to a discussion; for example, in think pair share activities
asking relevant questions and making connections with personal experiences and the contributions of others
understanding how to disagree or respectfully offer an alternative

entry_focuses: Listen,paraphrase and clarify
Connect statements,opinions and respectful alternatives
Give,follow and repair actual instructions
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide complete conversation/direction cards, missing-object clarification and quiet-library/garden opinion discussion. Original paper-shape directions need only paper,pencil; no cutting. Observe actual listening/restating, adding reason/action, giving/receiving directions and respectful disagreement. AAC/access/prompt support recorded; no forced eye contact.

codes.descriptor: identify the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts

elaborations.text: identifying the purpose of texts written by First Nations Australian authors
identifying the audience of advertisements and signs

entry_focuses: Identify imaginative,informative and persuasive purposes
Infer intended audience from whole-text clues
Discuss a named First Nations author’s purpose
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide three complete same-topic text samples plus twoactual signs/advertisement messages with explicit intended readers. Correct poster=form not inherent purpose. Adult supplies actual Open Your Heart to Country by Jasmine Seymour and its authorised ABC reading or lawful book; source-bounded brief summary is explicitly not fullbook/art observation. Discuss invitation/connection rather than infer onlyentertain or culturefromidentity.

codes.descriptor: read texts with phrasing and fluency, using phonic and word knowledge, and monitoring meaning by re-reading and self-correcting

elaborations.text: using phonic (sound-letter) and morphemic knowledge, and knowledge of high-frequency words when decoding text
monitoring own reading, self-correcting or reading back, re-reading when meaning does not make sense

entry_focuses: Read full printed words using phonics,morphemes and known words
Read connected phrases naturally with punctuation
Monitor,reread and self-correct against actual print
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide full original short passages and words with taught patterns/base+suffix/compound, phrasing variants and scripted adult reading slips. Adult may model a different line; do not read assessed target before independent decoding. Fix retained trywordthatfitsmeaning to print-first decoding. Actual observed rereading/selfcorrection without speed/accent norms; contextchecksmeaning after wordreading.

codes.descriptor: use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning

elaborations.text: listening for specific information and providing key facts or points from an informative or persuasive text
listening and responding to detailed instructions
integrating information from print, images and prior knowledge to make supportable inferences
identifying the main idea of a text
predicting vocabulary that is likely to be in a text, based on the topic and the purpose of the text; for example, predicting that “station” and “arrive” would be in a text recounting a train journey
using prior knowledge to make and confirm predictions when reading a text
using graphic organisers to represent the connections between characters, order of events or sequence of information

entry_focuses: Visualise,predict and connect using clues
Build literal/inferred meaning from words and a real picture
Summarise,question and repair meaning with an organiser
codes.status: READY TO DRAFT subject to independent plan review
codes.complete_stimuli: Provide a complete original station/seed-return story and facts/directions, plus actual existing feeder image inspected by root. Separate visibleclues,writtendetails,inference,unknown. Supply native sequence and evidenceorganisers. Listen to statedfacts/instructions; predict vocabulary fromactualtitle/topic thenconfirm notassume. Noimageguessingforreading and nofood/wildlifeactionrequired.
